note: Re-judged 2026-11-10 by an independent judge after a comment-only change to TestPortEncodingFollowsSection3131 (assertions, fixtures and the selectorsToWire/PortSelector.Wire producers byte-identical). The earlier enforced verdict was too wide. The test drives one fixture, protocol 0 with an ANY port, so it proves the all-ports-allowed encoding (ANY -> Start Port 0) and that the encoder can emit a non-zero port (TCP 443). It cannot fail on the 'protocols for which port is undefined' clause for any protocol other than 0, and Ze does not comply there: ipsec.checkPortProgrammable refuses a single port only when proto == 0, and engine.programmableSelector/intersectPort narrow away a specific port only under protocol 0, so a selector such as protocol 47 (GRE) with port 443, configured or proposed by a peer, reaches selectorsToWire and is emitted as 443/443 where RFC 7296 Section 3.13.1 says the field MUST be zero. Half the requirement is proven; the other half is a code defect.
